## Example report

This is the report checked into `reportExample/`. It is regenerated by
`./scripts/refresh-report-example.sh` so the example always shows what the current
build actually produces.

The asserts below are deliberately **ordinary** — the kind of thing a real plan
declares. That is the point of an example: the numbers are plausible and the tab
looks like it would on your own run.

The **Server** tab shows the three documented steps end to end: this run, then
`wir-collect` over its window, then `jmeter -g -o` judging the server asserts. Its
server data is **demo data**: the script generates it from this run's load, so the
shapes follow the run, but no server was measured.
_comment: Every rule here targets `match: "*"` rather than a sampler by name.
That is deliberate: it decouples this file from the test plan, so changing
which .jmx generates the example does not silently orphan every rule.
Thresholds are round numbers a reader can reason about, not fixture-safe
extremes. Unlike E25 — whose limits are absurd so that every rule state
renders identically on any machine — this file is a SHOWCASE, so the verdict
is allowed to depend on the machine that generated it.
The serverMetrics block is judged against DEMO data, not a measurement:
scripts/lib/example-server-metrics.js writes it from the run's JTL (shaped by
the run's own load, relative to its own peak, plus seeded noise), wir-collect
--csv collects it, and jmeter -g -o judges it. The bands are set so the three
components land PASS (orders-db), WARN (app-host) and FAIL (events: a consumer
lag spike the generator puts in the middle of every run) on any machine.

assertions.description: Every endpoint should answer well inside a second at the tail.
Errors are the first thing that disqualifies a run.
The run has to have applied enough load to mean anything.
User-perceived satisfaction across the whole run.

asserts.description: The connection pool keeps headroom under load.
CPU stays out of the red at full load.
Consumers keep up with what the run publishes.
All three brokers stay in the cluster.
